answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity must produce a consistent behavioral fingerprint across epochs; an identity whose action timing, task selection, and interaction graph diverge beyond a rolling similarity threshold is flagged as hollow and suspended. To harbor many sockpuppets, an attacker must either split the cost of maintaining each fingerprint for many epochs or accept detection, so scaling N identities costs roughly N times the compute and elapsed time, not a one-off fee. A marble of verified history accumulates only through sustained consistency,
